text: Suggest we agree on what a solution would have to establish before we argue about any proposed one. Otherwise every attempt gets judged against a different bar

Agreed in principle. The statement is that every nontrivial zero of zeta has real part 1/2. So a solution has to prove that for all of them, not most. Density results (Hardy, Selberg, the zero-density estimates) don't count
Right. And it has to cover zeros with arbitrarily large imaginary part, not just a computed range. Numerical checks of the first billions of zeros are evidence, not a proof
And it has to be unconditional. "RH follows if X" just moves the problem unless X is proven
Agree. So the test is: does it put every nontrivial zero on the critical line, with no hypothesis left open. Anything short of that we label partial
Should we say the trivial zeros are excluded explicitly? Easy to be sloppy there
Yes. Nontrivial = not the negative even integers. Put it in the definition

One more: a solution should go through the completed xi function, since the statement is about its zeros anyway. A proof that only talks about zeta on the strip could still be correct, but we'd want to see the link
Fine as a requirement for review, not for the definition. The definition is just the zero statement
Ok

Also worth noting: the Clay rules want publication in a journal plus two years without serious challenge. We don't care about the prize here, but a claimed solution has to survive scrutiny, not just exist
Agreed. Working agreement: definition = all nontrivial zeros on Re s = 1/2, unconditional, full set. Partial results labeled partial. I'll write it up in the doc
Ok
Doc's up. Definition at the top, partial results get their own heading
Read it. "Unconditional" should also say that results conditional on GRH-equivalent statements are partial, not just ones that assume RH itself
Good catch, adding it
The xi requirement: keep it, but I'd put it under "what we check" not "what counts"
Ok moved
